question: At the same later simulator state, does reused L0 change the relative selected-return quality of multitask versus scratch compared with a freshly drawn library?

budget.notes: Counts every intended simulator action: training collection, one reference prefix to t=12 per reset group, reset-plus-prefix replay before every candidate, and 16-step shared realizations. Resets are not steps. Training forwards are not imagined. make_planner uncertainty_penalty=0 adds no ensemble inferences. Direct .state mutation is not counted because it is not registered.

restoration.source_supports_determinism: H14/H15 already require reset(seed) observation and raw-state identity at t=0. MCC dense-height wrapper forces goal terminated=False. TimeLimit is 200; prefix 12 plus horizon 16 cannot truncate. Inner MCC physics is a deterministic map of (position, velocity, action).

identifiability.closed_loop_occupancy: controlled by shared model-independent prefixes; not measured as a controller occupancy
identifiability.positive_d_means: At sampled common later states, multitask-minus-scratch selected return is larger under L0 than under redraw.
identifiability.positive_d_does_not_mean: H14/H15 trajectory cause, compounding error, general control, cross-family transfer, learning-to-learn, or AGI.
